bull.b: Control of 26 MW of interconnected power and a very low blended energy cost can support mining margins over the next several quarters. This infrastructure also gives PowerCompute a durable operating base for expanding Bitcoin mining or eventually developing higher-performance computing workloads.

Lower unit energy costs and a mining margin above 50% indicate materially improved operating economics compared with the prior year. If maintained, this creates more cash-generation potential from existing capacity and improves resilience against ordinary fluctuations in mining revenue.

The sharp reduction in secured debt materially lowers interest burden, collateral risk, and refinancing pressure. Eliminating the Bitcoin-backed facility also leaves the company with greater control over its digital assets, improving financial flexibility for miner upgrades and working-capital needs.

bear.b: Persistent operating losses and negative cash generation weaken the company’s ability to fund expansion internally. Continued cash outflow can increase reliance on equity issuance, debt, or asset sales, while the lack of consistent profitability makes a durable operating turnaround essential to financial stability.

PowerCompute remains closely tied to Bitcoin prices because mining revenue can fall even when production rises. Variable power rates add another source of uncertainty, making margins and cash generation difficult to forecast and leaving the business exposed to prolonged weakness in cryptocurrency economics.

The delisting determination is a structural corporate risk that could impair trading liquidity, investor access, and financing flexibility if the listing is not preserved. Those effects could make it harder to raise capital or support growth even if mining operations continue improving.
